correctness.rationale: The nonlinear norm equals the maximum spectral norm of ball-selector matrices because maxima and suprema commute and each nonnegative selector has a nonnegative leading singular vector. An independently reconstructible 385-case rational certificate checks all graph ball rows from edge sets, 374 strict Sylvester inequalities and 11 winning exact characteristic polynomials. Algebraic root comparisons isolate the global sharp values. Irreducibility of each winning Gram matrix and explicit Perron eigenvectors classify all optimizing moduli; strict comparisons of distinct ball averages establish active-row consistency. No infinite quantification over graph order is asserted.

value.rationale: The finite result is a natural complete classification at the first order with six connected graph types. Beyond the already-published complete/star entries, it determines four previously unverified class constants, exact optimizer moduli and a striking two-pair coincidence across nonisomorphic graph types. It supplies precise minimal benchmarks for centered nonlinear maximal inequalities and tests whether norm invariants distinguish graphs. No extension to unmotivated larger finite slices is made.
